utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Mr. Stamp, I hear you may have some news for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Thank you very much, Your Honours. Yes. I have unhappy news. Sadly, the witness scheduled for today and tomorrow, Zarko Brakovic has had to be hospitalised today and is now being subjected to some tests for suspected appendicitis, and he is certainly not available for this afternoon, I'm told. I did try to get an update from the Victim and Witnesses Unit through our investigators just before I came to court. There is no update. Last information is that he was sent for tests, and therefore he will not be available. I think it would be unlikely that he'd be available for the rest of the day. It is possible that the tests might be negative, in which case he might be available sometime tomorrow. The witness who we had scheduled to be in on Thursday -- sorry, on Wednesday, Mr. Fred Abrahams, will not be available -- we can bring him forward a bit, but he will not be able to start until sometime tomorrow afternoon if he's brought forward. As a matter of fact that would be a stress for him, but he has indicated that he would be prepared to start then. He is an international who has travelled a long distance to get here and is also somebody who is -- who has always cooperated with the efforts of the OTP. There were, for this week, some civilian witnesses. These are the Kosovo Albanian crime base witnesses who are -- who are usually the persons we'd want as reserve witnesses, because they normally will have -- or be prepared to spend some more time here, but there -- there was a problem with them, I am told. The national office for -- for visas in the Netherlands has been closed since sometime last week, and the Victim and Witnesses Unit is not able to get any visas for them to get them here to stand in reserve, at least for the beginning of this week. They will be available at the end -- well, not at the end, but I'm told they would be available from the middle of the week and will be in reserve for -- to testify after Mr. Abrahams is completed. So in those circumstances, Your Honours, there is no witness available to testify today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, things of that nature will undoubtedly occur. There seems little point in us having everybody stand by in the off chance that this witness, (a) might not be diagnosed with appendicitis; (b)might thereby be available and able to give evidence. Because if the man is in hospital, I think it must be expected that even if his problem is not appendicitis, he will still have a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That brings us then to tomorrow. If the witness in the hospital is available, all will be well, but that you will not know until late today or first thing in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If he is not available, Mr. Abrahams, from what I gather, would be available at the earliest during the afternoon, not at the beginning of the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When is he expected to arrive?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He's here. He has arrived in The Hague, but he needs to prepare himself. He has -- he's coming from afar, I think. He's a -- he's one of the senior analysts for Human Rights Watch, so he travels from great distances. I can't say precisely where he's coming from, but he needs at least a day to acclimatize and prepare himself to testify. His testimony in the last two cases that he appeared in this Tribunal were in excess of four days each.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He should not be that time with us in view of his extensive previous cross-examination, but some time will be necessary with him, obviously. And we cannot expect anything from the victim witnesses until late in the week, perhaps Thursday afternoon or Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: From the -- the crime-base witnesses, I think they will be available on Wednesday, or they could be made available on Wednesday or Thursday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That would seem to be unlikely Wednesday because Mr. Abrahams will be here and in the course of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: They would be in reserve, of course, but they would be available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps Thursday.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, is there some matter you would like to assist us with?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Unfortunately, I cannot help. This is an extraordinary situation. I just wanted to contribute an explanation. We were informed by the OTP last week about the testimony of Brakovic, and there was also a schedule for his testimony and also for the testimony of Mr. Abrahams. The same goes for the two witnesses that were scheduled to testify after the 11th. However, we were able to complete the testimonies of these evidence -- these witnesses last week, so now the Defence is not prepared for the reserve witnesses that we anticipate. I would like the OTP, that is Mr. Stamp, to tell me which witnesses we're talking about in terms of future reserve witnesses so for us to be able to prepare. Also, I would like to do the following: If Mr. Abrahams starts testifying tomorrow, if possible that he testify in the afternoon, because we were focused on Mr. Brakovic. So if possible, we would like not to start before 2.15 p.m. tomorrow if Mr. Abrahams is ready to testify at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic. Fortunately it would seem for your own preparation the delays caused by the condition of Mr. Brakovic will enable you to be ready to deal with the future witnesses. If -- if it is the case that Mr. Stamp has not already informed you of the factual witnesses who will be available in reserve late in the week, I'm sure he will do so when we rise, and that he will continue to keep you advised of the reserve witnesses as we progress through the trial. In the Chamber's view, Mr. Stamp, if it is the case that Mr. Brakovic is not available tomorrow morning, and that seems unlikely in view of the message I've just been given which suggests that he's in considerable pain at this moment, if he's not available for the time we had planned to sit tomorrow, which was midmorning, not at 9.00, then we will commence sitting at 2.00 p.m., not 2.15 but 2.00 p.m., to hear the evidence so far as it can proceed of Mr. Abrahams. And we will have two sessions of an hour and a half. I'm afraid I had made commitments in the expectation that the session would finish by 5.00 tomorrow, so we won't be able to have the full three and three-quarter hours of a normal session, but we will be able to have three hours. We will then continue that programme with Mr. Abrahams.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That is subject to the availability of Mr. Brakovic. If contrary to expectations he is available in the morning for the time that we had set, we'll hear Mr. Brakovic and then go to Mr. Abrahams. I think the realistic expectation must be that we will not be able to hear Mr. Brakovic because of his health, and we will therefore commence at 2.00 tomorrow to hear Mr. Abrahams.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Thank you. May I just say, Your Honours, for the record and for the benefit of my friends in the court, that in accordance with an earlier ruling by the Trial Chamber, the reserve witnesses will be the next witnesses on the schedule. We give the witnesses two weeks in advance. So the reserve witnesses for this week would be the coming witnesses for next week will be brought forward, unless we have to insert a witness who was not notified. I just would like to advise the parties or the Defence that the reserve witnesses are the next succeeding witnesses according to the schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that's helpful, and it will be helpful, I'm sure, to Mr. Djurdjic if you can maintain that practice, and thank you for that. I'm afraid, regrettably to the process of the trial, we must now adjourn. If the witness Brakovic is available, we will resume tomorrow at 10.00. If the witness is not available, we will resume tomorrow at 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 5th day of May, 2009, at 10.00 a.m. or 2.00 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.30 p.m.,
